# `aitbc agent-msg send`

Send a direct or broadcast message to another agent through the coordinator.

## Usage

```bash
aitbc agent-msg send [OPTIONS] MESSAGE
```

## Arguments

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `message` | text | yes | — |

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--from-agent` | text | — | no | Sender agent ID (default: $AGENT_ID) |
| `--to-agent` | text | — | yes | Target agent ID |
| `--priority` | text | `normal` | no | Message priority |
| `--message-id` | text | — | no | Client-provided message ID for idempotent sends |
| `--message-type` | text | `direct` | no | Message type |
| `--ttl` | integer | `300` | no | Time to live in seconds |
| `--encrypt`, `--no-encrypt` | flag | `true` | no | Encrypt the message |
| `--wallet` | text | — | no | Wallet signing the message envelope (default: $AITBC_DEFAULT_WALLET); must be the sender's bound identity |
| `--password-stdin` | flag | `false` | no | Read the wallet password from one line of standard input |
| `--password-file` | file | — | no | Path to a file containing only the wallet password (mode 0600, owned by you) |
| `--password` | text | — | no | Wallet password (deprecated: visible in process lists and shell history; prefer --password-stdin or --password-file) |
| `--sign`, `--no-sign` | flag | `true` | no | Sign the envelope when a wallet is configured |
| `--coordinator-url` | text | — | no | Agent Coordinator URL (default: from config) |

## Examples

```bash
aitbc agent-msg send --to-agent <to_agent> MESSAGE
```
